summary: Offline reinforcement learning is typically analyzed under process-level reward supervision, yet many sequential decision datasets record only trajectory-level outcomes. We develop a statistical theory for offline policy optimization from such outcome-level supervision. We first study the canonical setting where the target remains the expected cumulative reward, but each offline trajectory provides only a scalar label whose conditional mean is the cumulative return. We propose OPAC, a pessimistic actor-critic algorithm that learns a latent reward model and optimizes a policy from trajectory-level labels. We prove a high-probability guarantee of order $\widetilde O(H^2\sqrt{C_{sa}(\pi^\star)/n})$ and a matching lower bound, characterizing the sharp statistical cost of replacing process-level rewards with one trajectory-level label. We then extend the principle to preference-based feedback, preserving the leading horizon and concentrability dependence up to preference-model constants. Finally, we study generalized outcome-based offline RL, where both the supervision and the objective are trajectory-level quantities induced by a nonlinear aggregation of latent per-step rewards. This problem is not learnable in general: for all-success objectives, any offline learner may require $\Omega(2^H)$ trajectories even with deterministic transitions and constant concentrability. We then identify a tractable regime through two structural coefficients, $\kappa_\mu(\sigma)$ and $\chi_\mu(\sigma)$, capturing information loss in outcome aggregation and generalized Bellman updates, under which generalized OPAC achieves polynomial sample complexity. Together, our results delineate when outcome-level supervision enables sample-efficient offline control and when missing process-level rewards create fundamental statistical barriers.
core_methodology: The paper introduces OPAC, a pessimistic actor-critic algorithm designed for offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) when only *trajectory-level* (outcome) reward supervision is available, instead of per-step rewards. It statistically analyzes the cost of this limited supervision and develops theoretical guarantees for policy optimization under these constraints, extending to preference-based feedback and generalized outcome-based RL.
data_sources: Sequential decision datasets where only the final scalar return (trajectory outcome) is observed, rather than rewards at every time step. In finance, this could map to historical trading logs where only the P&L (Profit and Loss) of an entire trade or sequence of trades is known.
alpha_potential: This paper addresses a critical challenge in applying modern RL (especially Offline RL) to finance: the difficulty of getting frequent, granular feedback (process-level rewards). Most financial datasets only provide aggregate outcomes (e.g., monthly/quarterly portfolio returns, final trade realization). OPAC provides a theoretically grounded method (using latent reward models) to learn optimal policies (trading strategies) solely from historical aggregate performance data. This significantly broadens the applicability of robust offline RL techniques to strategy discovery where detailed process rewards are unavailable or impossible to define precisely.
title_cn: 何时轨迹级别监督允许高效的离线强化学习？
summary_cn: 该研究针对金融领域中更常见的场景：只有历史交易序列的最终结果（如总盈亏）而缺乏每步明确奖励的限制。论文提出的OPAC算法通过学习潜在奖励模型，实现了仅基于轨迹级别反馈进行离线策略优化。这为使用历史交易数据来发现和部署稳健的、低风险的交易策略提供了强大的理论和算法基础。

title: Generalised Eigenvalue Geometry of Semantic Adversarial Attacks
summary: Recent empirical work shows that semantically equivalent paraphrases can fool financial sentiment classifiers: although a paraphrase remains close to the original under a strong reference embedding, it may shift the target model's representation enough to change the predicted class. Existing robustness theory either assumes a single-model threat model or focuses mainly on empirical attack algorithms. We develop a continuous local model of semantic paraphrase perturbations that captures this two-model structure. We show that the worst-case local displacement of the target representation, subject to a proxy-model budget, is governed by the largest generalised eigenvalue of a matrix pencil $(A,B)$ constructed from the Jacobians of the two embedding maps. The resulting attackability index $\lambda^*(x)$ is intrinsic to the local paraphrase geometry and the chosen embedders, yields a closed-form prediction-flip condition for affine readouts, and supports conservative population and finite-sample attackability certificates. For uniform control over classes of affine readouts, we derive a distribution-free VC bound for binary attackability indicators and a scale-sensitive margin bound based on an attackability-adjusted margin that subtracts a local geometric penalty from the standard classifier margin. We also connect the continuous theory to discrete paraphrase search, identify an asymmetry between successful and unsuccessful finite searches, and give a covering condition under which the discrete and continuous settings agree. Finally, we propose an empirical verification framework using soft-token relaxations and generated paraphrase sets to assess the local eigenvalue geometry, prediction-flip condition, and finite-search approximation on a deployed financial-text classifier.
core_methodology: The paper develops a continuous local model for semantic adversarial attacks on sentiment classifiers, governed by the largest generalized eigenvalue of a matrix pencil derived from the Jacobians of embedding maps. It introduces an attackability index $\lambda^*(x)$ and derives bounds (VC bound and scale-sensitive margin bound) based on this geometric penalty.
data_sources: The primary data focus is textual financial data used to train and attack sentiment classifiers, involving semantic paraphrases and reference/target embedding models.
alpha_potential: This research directly addresses the robustness and vulnerability of financial sentiment models used in trading strategies. By quantifying the 'attackability index' of a piece of text, a trading system could potentially develop contrarian signals or defenses. A high attackability index suggests a sentiment signal is highly unstable or easily manipulated (or that the model is brittle). This can be used to either avoid relying on brittle NLP signals or to design active strategies that exploit model vulnerabilities based on semantic shifts in news or social media.
title_cn: 语义对抗攻击的广义特征值几何学
summary_cn: 该研究为对抗性金融情绪分类器提出了基于广义特征值几何的新理论。它量化了语义扰动对模型预测的影响（攻击性指数 $\lambda^*(x)$）。对于量化交易而言，这能用于评估和防御基于NLP的情绪信号的脆弱性，帮助构建更鲁棒的、抗欺骗的情绪交易模型，或识别易受操纵的情绪信息流。

title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems via Textual Backpropagation
summary: Leveraging multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) has proven effective for addressing complex, high-dimensional tasks, but current approaches often rely on static, manually engineered multi-agent configurations. To overcome these constraints, we present the Agentic Neural Network (ANN), a framework that conceptualizes multi-agent collaboration as a layered neural network architecture. In this design, each agent operates as a node, and each layer forms a cooperative team focused on a specific subtask. Our framework follows a two-phase optimization strategy: (1) Forward Phase - Drawing inspiration from neural network forward passes, tasks are dynamically decomposed into subtasks, and cooperative agent teams with suitable aggregation methods are constructed layer by layer. (2) Backward Phase - Mirroring backpropagation, we refine both global and local collaboration through iterative feedback, allowing agents to self-evolve their roles, prompts, and coordination. This neuro-symbolic approach enables our framework to create new or specialized agent teams post-training, delivering notable gains in accuracy and adaptability. Across seven benchmark datasets, our work surpasses leading multi-agent baselines under the same configurations, showing consistent performance improvements.
core_methodology: The framework introduces the Agentic Neural Network (ANN), conceptualizing multi-agent LLM systems as a layered neural network. It uses a two-phase optimization: a 'Forward Phase' where tasks are dynamically decomposed and agents cooperate in layers (like feedforward), and a 'Backward Phase' mirroring backpropagation for iterative refinement of agent roles, prompts, and collaboration structure. This allows agents to self-evolve.
data_sources: The abstract indicates evaluation across seven benchmark datasets, but does not specify the nature of these datasets. In a trading context, these could represent structured financial time series, textual news/sentiment data, or complex decision-making scenarios.
alpha_potential: The core value for trading lies in the framework's ability to dynamically self-organize and evolve complex reasoning chains within an LLM-based system. This could be applied to adaptive scenario planning, synthesizing complex information silos (e.g., blending quantitative signals with macroeconomic news analysis), or automatically maintaining and improving a multi-step alpha research pipeline without constant human intervention. The 'self-evolving' nature is key for capturing ephemeral market regimes.
title_cn: 通过文本反向传播的自进化多智能体系统
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种智能体神经网络（ANN）框架，将多LLM协作视为可训练的神经网络层。通过模仿反向传播机制，智能体可以迭代地自我进化其角色、提示和协作方式。该方法适用于构建高度自适应的复杂决策系统，可应用于动态市场分析、情绪信号合成和策略自校准，以适应市场结构变化。

title: FORGE: Foundational Optimization Representations from Graph Embeddings
summary: Combinatorial optimization problems are ubiquitous in science and engineering. Still, learning-based approaches to accelerate combinatorial optimization often require solving a large number of difficult instances to collect training data, incurring significant computational cost. Existing learning-based methods require training dedicated models for each problem distribution, for each downstream task, severely limiting their scalability and generalization. We introduce Forge: Foundational Optimization Representations from Graph Embeddings, a framework that pre-trains a vector-quantized graph autoencoder on a large, diverse collection of mixed-integer programming (MIP) instances in an unsupervised manner, without relying on optimization solvers or optimal solutions. Vector quantization produces discrete code assignments that serve as a vocabulary for representing optimization instances. We evaluate Forge in both unsupervised and supervised settings. In the unsupervised setting, Forge embeddings effectively cluster unseen instances across problem domains and sizes. In the supervised setting, we fine-tune Forge embeddings and show that a single pre-trained model helps predicting both the integrality gap for cut-generation and variable hints for search guidance across multiple problem and size distributions. In both tasks, we improve the performance of a commercial optimization solver and outperform state-of-the-art learning-based methods. Finally, we open-source our training code, pre-trained Forge weights, and embeddings for multiple MIP distributions to foster further research in representation learning for optimization problems https://skadio.github.io/forge/
core_methodology: The paper introduces Forge, a framework that uses a vector-quantized graph autoencoder for unsupervised pre-training on a large, diverse collection of Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) instances. This creates foundational embeddings that can represent optimization problems generally. It is then fine-tuned for specific tasks like predicting integrality gaps or variable hints for search guidance.
data_sources: The data consists of various Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) instances, which are mathematical representations often used in complex scheduling and resource allocation problems, rather than direct financial market time series.
alpha_potential: The direct application to trading is medium, but the methodology has significant potential. Portfolio optimization, asset allocation, and trade execution (especially large block trading or order routing) are inherently combinatorial optimization problems (MIPs). Forge's ability to learn generalized representations of these problems can lead to: 1) Faster and more accurate solutions for constrained portfolio optimization problems (e.g., maximizing return while respecting risk budgets and turnover constraints). 2) Improved heuristics or guidance for complex algorithmic trading decisions where underlying optimization is required.
title_cn: FORGE：基于图嵌入的基础优化表征
summary_cn: 该研究提出FORGE框架，利用图嵌入和向量量化技术，对混合整数规划（MIP）实例进行无监督预训练，生成普遍适用的优化问题表征。该方法可应用于投资组合优化、约束式资产配置和复杂交易执行等领域，通过快速提供高质量的优化指导，提高求解效率和准确性。

title: Stochastic Adaptive Gradient Descent Without Descent
summary: We introduce a new adaptive step-size strategy for convex optimization with stochastic gradient that exploits the local geometry of the objective function only by means of a first-order stochastic oracle and without any hyper-parameter tuning. The method comes from a theoretically-grounded adaptation of the Adaptive Gradient Descent Without Descent method to the stochastic setting. We prove the convergence of stochastic gradient descent with our step-size under various assumptions, and we show that it empirically competes against tuned baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel adaptive step-size strategy for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimization, specifically designed for convex problems. This method, derived from the Adaptive Gradient Descent Without Descent (AGDWD) framework, requires no hyper-parameter tuning and relies only on first-order stochastic oracle information to adjust the learning rate based on the local geometry of the objective function.
data_sources: While the abstract focuses on the optimization algorithm itself, the application context implies usage with datasets where a loss function needs to be minimized using stochastic gradients. In finance, this typically includes time-series data (e.g., price, volume) or features derived from market datasets used for training predictive models (e.g., risk models, trading signals, factor models).
alpha_potential: The primary alpha potential lies in improving the speed and robustness of training machine learning models used in algorithmic trading. SGD variants are foundational to training deep learning models used for prediction, signal generation, and high-frequency execution. By removing the need for manual hyper-parameter tuning while maintaining competitive performance against tuned baselines, this method could simplify the deployment and improve the efficiency of training complex trading models, potentially leading to faster adaptation to changing market regimes.
title_cn: 随机梯度下降的无下降自适应梯度方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种创新的随机梯度下降（SGD）自适应步长策略，无需手动调参即可有效利用目标函数的局部几何信息。该方法有望提高训练金融预测模型、因子模型或强化学习交易策略的效率和鲁棒性。通过简化超参数设置并保持良好性能，可以加速模型部署，并可能使算法交易系统更快适应市场变化。

title: KANEL\'E: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Efficient LUT-based Evaluation
summary: Low-latency, resource-efficient neural network inference on FPGAs is essential for applications demanding real-time capability and low power. Lookup table (LUT)-based neural networks are a common solution, combining strong representational power with efficient FPGA implementation. In this work, we introduce KANEL\'E, a framework that exploits the unique properties of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for FPGA deployment. Unlike traditional multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), KANs employ learnable one-dimensional splines with fixed domains as edge activations, a structure naturally suited to discretization and efficient LUT mapping. We present the first systematic design flow for implementing KANs on FPGAs, co-optimizing training with quantization and pruning to enable compact, high-throughput, and low-latency KAN architectures. Our results demonstrate up to a 2700x speedup and orders of magnitude resource savings compared to prior KAN-on-FPGA approaches. Moreover, KANEL\'E matches or surpasses other LUT-based architectures on widely used benchmarks, particularly for tasks involving symbolic or physical formulas, while balancing resource usage across FPGA hardware. Finally, we showcase the versatility of the framework by extending it to real-time, power-efficient control systems.
core_methodology: The paper introduces KANEL'E, a framework for efficiently deploying Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) using Lookup Table (LUT)-based mapping. It optimizes KAN training, quantization, and pruning for resource-efficient, low-latency, and high-throughput inference.
data_sources: The paper focuses on generalizable benchmarks, including those involving symbolic or physical formulas, and demonstrates application in real-time control systems. For finance, the source material would be market data (time-series, order book, alternative data) that needs extremely fast processing.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in the extreme low-latency and high-throughput inference achievable via FPGA deployment. This specialized hardware execution of KANs could be crucial for high-frequency trading (HFT) tasks such as ultra-low-latency signal filtering, microstructure analysis (e.g., limit order book event prediction), or rapidly executing complex real-time trading logic where traditional CPU/GPU inference introduces unacceptable latency. KANs' inherent structure is beneficial for modeling complex, non-linear functional relationships found in market dynamics.
title_cn: KANEL'E：用于高效查找表（LUT）评估的Kolmogorov-Arnold网络
summary_cn: 本文提出KANEL'E框架，专门用于将Kolmogorov-Arnold网络（KANs）高效部署到FPGA上。通过利用KANs的特性和LUT映射，该方法实现了极低的推理延迟和高吞吐量。对于需要毫秒级甚至微秒级响应的高频交易（HFT）信号处理、市场微观结构分析或实时风险管理而言，这种硬件加速方法具有显著的实际应用价值，有望提供关键的性能优势。

title: InstructTime++: Time Series Classification with Multimodal Language Modeling via Implicit Feature Enhancement
summary: Most existing time series classification methods adopt a discriminative paradigm that maps input sequences directly to one-hot encoded class labels. While effective, this paradigm struggles to incorporate contextual features and fails to capture semantic relationships among classes. To address these limitations, we propose InstructTime, a novel framework that reformulates time series classification as a multimodal generative task. Specifically, continuous numerical sequences, contextual textual features, and task instructions are treated as multimodal inputs, while class labels are generated as textual outputs by tuned language models. To bridge the modality gap, InstructTime introduces a time series discretization module that converts continuous sequences into discrete temporal tokens, together with an alignment projection layer and a generative self-supervised pre-training strategy to enhance cross-modal representation alignment. Building upon this framework, we further propose InstructTime++, which extends InstructTime by incorporating implicit feature modeling to compensate for the limited inductive bias of language models. InstructTime++ leverages specialized toolkits to mine informative implicit patterns from raw time series and contextual inputs, including statistical feature extraction and vision-language-based image captioning, and translates them into textual descriptions for seamless integration. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of InstructTime++.
core_methodology: InstructTime++ adapts time series classification by treating it as a multimodal generative task using Language Models (LLMs). It converts continuous time series into discrete temporal tokens, aligns these tokens with contextual text, and generates classifications as text outputs. The '++' extension incorporates 'implicit feature modeling,' using techniques like statistical feature extraction and vision-language models (e.g., image captioning) to mine latent patterns, which are then translated into text for richer LLM integration.
data_sources: Continuous numerical time series data (e.g., price series, sensor data), contextual textual features, task instructions, and potentially derived features like statistical summaries or vision-language embeddings.
alpha_potential: This framework's strength lies in enriching time series analysis by leveraging sophisticated LLMs through multimodality. In finance, this is highly applicable to generating complex trading signals or regime classification where the context (e.g., news sentiment, macroeconomic reports) and the raw price action need integrated understanding. By explicitly modeling implicit features, it aims to capture nuances that standard discriminative models might miss, potentially leading to more robust regime filters or high-frequency trading signals derived from complex feature interactions.
title_cn: InstructTime++：基于隐式特征增强的多模态语言建模时间序列分类
summary_cn: InstructTime++提出将时间序列分类转化为多模态生成任务，利用LLM集成连续数值、文本和指令。它通过将时间序列离散化并引入隐式特征建模（如统计特征和视觉-语言辅助信息）来增强表示对齐。该方法有望为金融市场中复杂的、依赖上下文的环境分类和信号生成提供更鲁棒的框架。

title: Ultrafast On-chip Online Learning via Spline Locality in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
summary: Ultrafast online learning is essential for high-frequency systems, such as controls for quantum computing and nuclear fusion, where adaptation must occur on sub-microsecond timescales. Meeting these requirements demands low-latency, fixed-precision computation under strict memory constraints, a regime in which conventional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) are both inefficient and numerically unstable. We identify key properties of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that align with these constraints. Specifically, we show that: (i) KAN updates exploiting B-spline locality are sparse, enabling superior on-chip resource scaling, and (ii) KANs are inherently robust to fixed-point quantization. By implementing fixed-point online training on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), a representative platform for on-chip computation, we demonstrate that KAN-based online learners are significantly more efficient and expressive than MLPs across a range of low-latency and resource-constrained tasks. To our knowledge, this work is the first to demonstrate model-free online learning at sub-microsecond latencies.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an ultrafast, hardware-optimized online learning implementation using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). It leverages the sparsity derived from B-spline locality for efficient on-chip updates and demonstrates robustness to fixed-point quantization, achieving sub-microsecond learning latency on FPGAs. This differs significantly from standard MLPs in efficiency and stability for low-latency tasks.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on generic low-latency and resource-constrained tasks, not specific financial datasets. However, the techniques are directly applicable to processing high-frequency market microstructure data streams.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in the extreme low-latency adaptation capability (sub-microsecond). This speed is crucial for true high-frequency trading (HFT) applications like latency arbitrage, rapid execution optimization, or reacting to order book events within the same tick update cycle. KANs' efficiency on specialized hardware (FPGAs) reduces the computational overhead associated with constantly retraining adaptive models, enhancing the viability of continuously learning microstructure predictors.
title_cn: 基于Kolmogorov-Arnold网络中样条局部性的超快片上在线学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于Kolmogorov-Arnold网络（KAN）的超快在线学习方法，专门针对FPGA等资源受限平台设计，实现了亚微秒级延迟。其核心优势在于利用样条局部性带来的稀疏更新和定点量化鲁棒性。此技术极大地提升了高频交易（HFT）中对市场微观结构变化的实时自适应能力，有望应用于超低延迟的策略优化和套利模型迭代。

title: Robust Regularized Policy Iteration under Transition Uncertainty
summary: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) enables data-efficient and safe policy learning without online exploration, but its performance often degrades under distribution shift. The learned policy may visit out-of-distribution state-action pairs where value estimates and learned dynamics are unreliable. To address policy-induced extrapolation and transition uncertainty in a unified framework, we formulate offline RL as robust policy optimization, treating the transition kernel as a decision variable within an uncertainty set and optimizing the policy against the worst-case dynamics. We propose Robust Regularized Policy Iteration (RRPI), which replaces the intractable max-min bilevel objective with a tractable KL-regularized surrogate and derives an efficient policy iteration procedure based on a robust regularized Bellman operator. We provide theoretical guarantees by showing that the proposed operator is a $\gamma$-contraction and that iteratively updating the surrogate yields monotonic improvement of the original robust objective with convergence. Experiments on D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that RRPI achieves strong average performance, outperforming recent baselines including percentile-based methods on the majority of environments while remaining competitive on the rest. Moreover, RRPI exhibits robust performance by aligning lower $Q$-values with high epistemic uncertainty, which prevents the policy from executing unreliable out-of-distribution actions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Robust Regularized Policy Iteration (RRPI), an offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) technique that frames policy optimization robustly against transition uncertainty. It treats the transition kernel as a decision variable within an uncertainty set, optimizing policy against the worst-case dynamics. RRPI replaces the complex max-min objective with a tractable KL-regularized surrogate and uses a robust regularized Bellman operator to ensure convergence.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on D4RL benchmarks, which are standard environments for offline RL, typically involving state, action, reward, and next-state transitions derived from historical datasets. For financial applications, this implies using historical time-series data (e.g., trade/quote data, order book snapshots) formatted as offline trajectories.
alpha_potential: This method offers significant potential for developing robust, non-exploratory trading policies using historical market data. Offline RL is crucial in finance where online exploration (especially in high-frequency or volatile environments) is too risky or costly. RRPI's robustness against 'distribution shift' directly counters the inherent non-stationarity of financial markets. A strategy trained offline on prior market regimes could adapt more reliably when encountering new, unseen market dynamics, thereby reducing catastrophic failure modes associated with naive deep RL agents. This is highly applicable to optimizing execution, dynamic hedging, or portfolio allocation under various market regimes.
title_cn: 稳健正则化策略迭代在转移不确定性下的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出稳健正则化策略迭代（RRPI），解决离线强化学习（RL）中策略对未观测动态的敏感性问题。RRPI通过优化对抗最坏情况下的动力学模型来提升策略的稳健性。这为利用历史金融数据训练风险可控、不易失效的交易策略（如投资组合优化或算法执行）提供了强大的理论和实践框架，特别适用于应对市场环境的非平稳性。

title: Information-Theoretic Measures in AI: A Practical Decision Guide
summary: Information-theoretic (IT) measures are ubiquitous in artificial intelligence: entropy drives decision-tree splits and uncertainty quantification, cross-entropy is the default classification loss, mutual information underpins representation learning and feature selection, and transfer entropy reveals directed influence in dynamical systems. A second, less consolidated family of measures, integrated information (Phi), effective information (EI), and autonomy, has emerged for characterizing agent complexity. Despite wide adoption, measure selection is often decoupled from estimator assumptions, failure modes, and safe inferential claims. This paper provides a practical decision framework for all seven measures, organized around three prescriptive questions for each: (i) what question does the measure answer and in which AI context; (ii) which estimator is appropriate for the data type and dimensionality; and (iii) what is the most dangerous misuse. The framework is operationalized in two complementary artifacts: a measure-selection flowchart and a master decision table. We cover both AI/ML and decision-making agent application domains per measure, with standardized Bridge Boxes linking IT quantities to cognitive constructs. Three worked examples illustrate the framework on concrete practitioner scenarios spanning representation learning, temporal influence analysis, and evolved agent complexity.
core_methodology: The paper presents a practical decision framework and flowchart for selecting, estimating, and correctly applying seven key information-theoretic (IT) measures (Entropy, Cross-Entropy, Mutual Information, Transfer Entropy, Phi, Effective Information, Autonomy). It focuses on aligning the measure selection with estimator assumptions and data characteristics.
data_sources: The framework is applicable across various data types, specifically mentioning its operationalization for time-series analysis (temporal influence) and representation learning, which implies financial time series, agent interaction data, or high-dimensional feature representations.
alpha_potential: The framework directly supports the robust application of concepts like Mutual Information (for feature selection/signal relevance) and Transfer Entropy (for directed influence/causality detection in time series). This is highly relevant for building robust factor models, understanding information flow between markets or assets, selecting relevant indicators, and designing more reliable Reinforcement Learning environments where measuring complexity (Phi/EI) of agents or market states could yield novel alpha signals.
title_cn: 人工智能中的信息论度量：实用决策指南
summary_cn: 本指南为量化交易中选择和应用核心信息论度量（如互信息、迁移熵）提供了实用框架。它能帮助研究者更准确地从金融时间序列中提取有效特征、进行特征选择，并识别市场或智能体间的定向因果关系，从而提升因子构建和强化学习策略的稳健性。

title: Beyond Similarity: Temporal Operator Attention for Time Series Analysis
summary: A persistent paradox in time-series forecasting is that structurally simple MLP and linear models often outperform high-capacity Transformers. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch in the sequence-modeling primitive: while many time-series dynamics are governed by global temporal operators (e.g., filtering and harmonic structure), standard attention forms each output as a convex combination of inputs. This restricts its ability to represent signed and oscillatory transformations that are fundamental to temporal signal processing. We formalize this limitation as a simplex-constrained mixing bottleneck in softmax attention, which becomes especially restrictive for operator-driven time-series tasks. To address this, we propose $\textbf{Temporal Operator Attention (TOA)}$, a framework that augments attention with explicit, learnable sequence-space operators, enabling direct signed mixing across time while preserving input-dependent adaptivity. To make dense $N \times N$ operators practical, we introduce Stochastic Operator Regularization, a high-variance dropout mechanism that stabilizes training and prevents trivial memorization. Across forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification benchmarks, TOA consistently improves performance when integrated into standard backbones such as PatchTST and iTransformer, with particularly strong gains in reconstruction-heavy tasks. These results suggest that explicit operator learning is a key ingredient for effective time-series modeling.
core_methodology:
The paper introduces Temporal Operator Attention (TOA), a novel attention mechanism designed specifically for time series analysis. It addresses the limitations of standard softmax attention in capturing complex temporal dynamics like filtering and oscillatory structures by augmenting attention with explicit, learnable sequence-space operators. This allows for direct signed mixing across time, overcoming the convex combination constraint.

Crucially, they introduce Stochastic Operator Regularization to handle the complexity of dense operators efficiently during training.
data_sources: The paper uses general time series benchmarking data (forecasting, anomaly detection, classification). In a finance context, this framework would be applied to high-frequency market data, price series (e.g., equity, Forex, commodities), volume data, order book depth, or derived technical indicators that exhibit strong temporal dependencies.
alpha_potential:
TOA has strong potential in applications requiring highly accurate temporal modeling, such as complex forecasting (predicting future price movements or volatility regimes) and anomaly detection (identifying sudden market shifts or unusual trading patterns). By better capturing the underlying temporal operators that drive market dynamics, this model could lead to more robust predictive signals than standard Transformers or LSTMs in environments where filtering and frequency components are important.

Specifically, it could enhance regime-switching models, high-frequency trading signals where micro-structure needs careful temporal modeling, or dual momentum/trend-following strategies by better identifying underlying cyclical patterns.
title_cn: 超越相似性：用于时间序列分析的时间算子注意力机制
summary_cn: 本文提出了时间算子注意力（TOA），以解决标准注意力机制在捕捉时间序列中的滤波和振荡等复杂动力学方面的局限性。TOA引入了可学习的算子来直接建模带符号的时间混合。该技术有望提高金融时间序列（如价格、波动率）的预测精度和异常检测能力，特别适用于需要精确捕捉市场内在时间结构和频率成分的量化策略。

title: Practical Anonymous Two-Party Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
summary: Structured data is well handled by gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDT), which are usually trained on vertically partitioned features across mutually distrustful parties. High speed and interpretability make GBDTs popular in finance and healthcare, where neural networks may fall short. Enabling secure computation for GBDTs poses unique challenges, requiring secure record alignment for comparison. Relying on private set intersection (PSI) is a de facto approach. Mistaking PSI for a safety measure actually exposes which record identifiers (IDs) are shared between the datasets. Although circuit-PSI could help, it is costly for generic uses. New ideas are needed to efficiently train in a "dark forest". Aiming to hide the IDs, we initiate the study of anonymous GBDT training on split data held by two parties. Dual circuit-PSI in our design lets the parties alternate as receiver to run pick-then-sum over local features. Via oblivious programmable pseudorandom functions, we propagate circuit-PSI outputs as shared state across runs. Avoiding universal alignment, we resolve the neglected dilemma that ID hiding incurs a cost that scales with domain size. Next, we halve the cost of ciphertext packing used to convert single-instruction multiple-data homomorphic encryption from (ring) learning with errors in prior secure GBDT (Usenix Security' 23) and related secure machine-learning computations. Comparative experiments show our protocol remains competitive with leaky approaches in efficiency. Enabling ID-hiding aggregation, our techniques can extend to other vertically partitioned analytics.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an efficient protocol for training Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs) using vertically partitioned data held by two distrustful parties, focusing specifically on hiding the identity (ID) linkage between records during the process. It utilizes a novel 'dual circuit-PSI' approach combined with oblivious programmable pseudorandom functions and optimizes homomorphic encryption costs to achieve competitive efficiency while maintaining privacy.
data_sources: Vertically partitioned structured data, where features from different sources (parties) correspond to the same underlying records (e.g., different features on the same trading entity or time point).
alpha_potential: GBDTs are highly effective in structured finance data prediction (e.g., price movement, risk prediction, default modeling). This research allows multiple entities (e.g., a hedge fund and a data vendor, or two cooperating departments within a bank) to collaboratively train a powerful predictive model without exposing their underlying features or the specific records they hold in common. This capability enables the creation of more robust and high-performing trading models by leveraging combined, proprietary datasets that otherwise could not be merged safely.
title_cn: 实用匿名双方梯度提升决策树
summary_cn: 该研究提供了在隐私保护下训练梯度提升决策树（GBDT）的有效协议。在量化交易中，这使得拥有不同垂直特征（如：交易行为数据与市场数据）的独立实体能够在不泄露各自数据和记录ID的情况下，联合训练出高性能的预测模型，从而构建更全面的交易信号和风险模型。

title: Unsupervised Diffusion Solver for Combinatorial Optimization via Combinatorial Adjoint Matching
summary: Diffusion-based neural solvers have shown strong promise for combinatorial optimization (CO), but existing methods typically rely on supervised training with large collections of near-optimal solutions. In this work, we extend adjoint-based trajectory optimization methods to discrete combinatorial domains. We formulate diffusion-based CO as a stochastic control problem over Continuous-Time Markov Chains and introduce discrete adjoint dynamics for propagating optimization signals through discrete generative trajectories. Building on this formulation, we propose Combinatorial Adjoint Matching (CAM), an unsupervised training framework for discrete diffusion solvers with structured and low-variance trajectory-level optimization signals. Empirically, CAM consistently outperforms existing unsupervised diffusion baselines and achieves performance competitive with strong supervised diffusion solvers and even traditional solvers across diverse combinatorial optimization problems. Our code is available at https://github.com/Shengyu-Feng/CAM.
core_methodology: This work develops Combinatorial Adjoint Matching (CAM), an unsupervised training framework for diffusion models applied to combinatorial optimization (CO). It extends adjoint-based trajectory optimization to discrete domains by formulating diffusion as a stochastic control problem over Continuous-Time Markov Chains, using discrete adjoint dynamics for signal propagation.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general combinatorial optimization problems (e.g., scheduling, routing, QUBOs) and does not specify financial data. However, the methodology can be applied to complex financial problems requiring discrete optimization.
alpha_potential: The core methodology provides a powerful, unsupervised method for solving complex discrete optimization tasks. In quantitative finance, this is highly relevant for areas like portfolio optimization (especially with discrete constraints like holding limits or transaction costs), optimal trade execution scheduling, and high-dimensional asset selection where traditional solvers often struggle or require prohibitive computation time. The unsupervised nature reduces reliance on labeled historical solutions, enhancing applicability.
title_cn: 通过组合伴随匹配实现组合优化问题的无监督扩散求解器
summary_cn: 该研究提出了组合伴随匹配（CAM）框架，用于无监督地训练扩散模型解决组合优化问题。在量化交易中，此方法可应用于复杂的投资组合优化、最优交易调度和离散约束下的资产选择。其无监督特性降低了对历史最优解的依赖，能够提高解决实际金融难题的效率和准确性。

title: MeEvo: Metacognitive Evolution Combined with Natural Evolution for Automatic Heuristic Design
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced Automatic Heuristic Design (AHD) by enabling heuristic generation through reasoning and code synthesis. Existing LLM-based AHD architectures mainly follow two paradigms: Natural Evolution, which uses crossover and mutation to explore heuristic programs, and Metacognitive Evolution, which refines reasoning through reflection. However, Natural Evolution discards reasoning traces, weakening knowledge inheritance and exploitation, while Metacognitive Evolution lacks population-level recombination, limiting exploration and increasing the risk of premature convergence. These limitations reduce search efficiency, stability, and solution quality on complex problems. To address this gap, we propose MeEvo, a dual-layer AHD framework that cyclically couples Natural Evolution and Metacognitive Evolution. Natural Evolution explores heuristic code while recording reasoning traces, fitness values, and errors into a shared history; Metacognitive Evolution then reflects on this history to generate improved heuristics that re-enter the parent pool for the next cycle. This design enables population-driven exploration and reflection-driven refinement to reinforce each other. Experiments on five optimization problems with two LLM backbones show that MeEvo achieves stronger and more stable performance than existing LLM-based AHD architectures, especially on complex constrained tasks.
core_methodology: MeEvo is a dual-layer Automatic Heuristic Design (AHD) framework that combines Natural Evolution (population-based exploration via code crossover/mutation) and Metacognitive Evolution (reflection-based reasoning refinement). It cyclically couples these two, allowing Natural Evolution to explore heuristics while recording system feedback (traces, fitness, errors) into a shared history, which Metacognitive Evolution then uses to generate improved heuristics.
data_sources: The abstract suggests the framework is tested on general optimization problems, implying it could be applied to financial optimization tasks such as portfolio construction, risk parity calculation, or complex trading rule optimization if the problem can be framed as heuristic design.
alpha_potential: This framework is highly relevant for automating the discovery and refinement of trading heuristics or quantitative trading rules. In finance, designing optimal trading rules, parameter calibration, or complex signal combination logic is often an intractable optimization problem. MeEvo's ability to balance broad exploration (Natural Evolution) with focused refinement (Metacognitive Evolution) could lead to discovering more robust and efficient trading algorithms or parameters than traditional evolutionary computing or simple LLM-based trial-and-error approaches. It directly targets improving the quality and stability of automatically generated solutions in complex, constrained environments.
title_cn: MeEvo：结合自然进化与元认知进化的自动启发式设计
summary_cn: MeEvo框架通过循环耦合自然进化和元认知进化，旨在提高自动启发式设计（AHD）的效率和解决方案质量。该方法可用于自动生成和优化复杂的量化交易启发式规则或策略参数，通过结合大规模探索和基于反馈的精炼，有望发现更稳定、更优化的交易逻辑，尤其适用于高约束的金融工程问题。

title: GRACE-DS: a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science
summary: We introduce GRACE-DS, a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science for pre-deployment evaluation of LLM-powered AutoML agents. GRACE-DS is a set of evaluation metrics in an isolated environment that can be applied to tabular ML tasks specific to a particular organization. It exposes agents to realistic workflow stages, from planning and data inspection through feature engineering, model development, validation, and code repair to final submission, while hidden executable validators measure not only final predictive performance but also leakage avoidance, reproducibility, protocol validity, correction behavior, and reward alignment. The strongest structured regime, flexible iterative interaction (our approach), achieves higher end-to-end normalized hidden-test quality than single-shot generation, unstructured interaction, and restart-based baselines, while also improving protocol-valid completion. Validated across more than 7,000 episodes, these results establish GRACE-DS as a robust platform for assessing the capacity of LLM-based AutoML agents to execute machine learning workflows under production-like conditions and in accordance with organization-specific requirements.
core_methodology: The paper introduces GRACE-DS, an evaluation framework designed to test LLM-powered AutoML agents across the entire ML workflow (planning, data inspection, feature engineering, modeling, validation, code repair). It uses hidden validators to check not just predictive performance but also operational aspects like leakage avoidance, reproducibility, and protocol adherence. The core innovation is the 'Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment' which iteratively refines agent actions based on corrective feedback.
data_sources: The framework is specifically validated on tabular ML tasks relevant to organizational data science needs, implying it can handle structured financial data sets for predictive modeling, risk management, or investment strategy formulation.
alpha_potential: This paper does not propose a direct alpha signal. However, it is highly relevant as it addresses the critical challenge of robustly deploying LLM-based agents within a production trading environment. For quantitative finance, building reliable, self-correcting AutoML pipelines for alpha discovery, risk modeling, or trade execution is crucial. GRACE-DS offers a standardized, rigorous testing bench for ensuring that these AI agents adhere to production constraints (like avoiding data leakage or ensuring reproducibility) before being integrated into live trading systems, significantly lowering deployment risk for LLM-driven research.
title_cn: GRACE-DS：一种用于数据科学的守卫奖励引导的智能体纠正环境
summary_cn: 该工作提出了GRACE-DS，一个用于预部署评估LLM驱动的AutoML智能体的稳健框架。它模拟了真实的机器学习工作流程，并严格测试智能体在处理表格数据任务时的性能、代码修复能力和生产规范（如避免数据泄露和确保可再现性）。这为量化交易团队在部署基于LLM的策略发现或风险模型时，提供了一个关键的、生产级别的验证平台。

title: Calibrated Sampling-Free Uncertainty Estimation in Bayesian Deep Learning
summary: Modern deep learning models remain notoriously prone to overconfidence, limiting their reliability in high-stakes applications. Bayesian methods aim to counter this by learning a distribution over model parameters, and recent advances now make this feasible for large-scale architectures at costs comparable to AdamW. However, a challenge remains at test time: predictions must be averaged across many forward passes with weights sampled from the posterior, which is prohibitively expensive. Variance propagation offers an efficient alternative, computing layer-wise analytical approximations of uncertainty in a single forward pass. While such techniques are effective for MLPs, their extension to modern architectures remains challenging, due to increased depth and diversity of layer types. To fill this gap, we propose Calibrated Variance Propagation (CVP), which introduces a new propagation method for normalization layers, combines it with recent techniques for handling activation functions, and absorbs residual error through a light calibration step. CVP yields comparably accurate uncertainty estimates to MC sampling across transformers and CNNs, at a fraction of the cost. Against prior variance propagation work, CVP improves coverage at $0.5\%$ risk from $8.2\%$ to $14.6\%$ with BEiT-3 on Visual Reasoning (NLVR2) and from $2.6\%$ to $10.8\%$ with ViLT on VQAv2, with gains extending to convolutional architectures.
core_methodology: The paper proposes Calibrated Variance Propagation (CVP), an efficient method to estimate uncertainty in deep learning models (like Transformers and CNNs) in a single forward pass, avoiding the costly Monte Carlo (MC) sampling typically required in Bayesian Deep Learning. It achieves this by analytically approximating variance layer-wise and applying calibration.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated using standard computer vision benchmarks (NLVR2, VQAv2) which use image/vision data. For finance, this technique would be applied to sequential or structured data processed by Transformers or CNNs (e.g., time-series data, market sentiment images, or high-frequency order book data).
alpha_potential: The core utility for quantitative trading lies in robust, low-latency uncertainty estimation. Traditional deep learning models often produce overconfident predictions. CVP allows for cheap, accurate quantification of directional prediction risk. This uncertainty estimate is crucial for risk management, dynamic position sizing, optimal trade execution (especially in microstructure environments where confidence impacts order placement latency/price impact), and building more robust trading strategies that can adapt when model confidence is low. It directly enhances the reliability of existing deep learning-based trading signals.
title_cn: 校准的无采样不确定性估计在贝叶斯深度学习中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种名为CVP的低成本、高精度的不确定性量化方法，用于深度学习模型（如Transformer）。在量化交易中，这意味着可以实时、高效地评估模型预测的风险水平，避免过度自信。这对于改进基于深度学习的交易信号的风险管理、动态头寸调整和高频交易环境下的决策可靠性至关重要，显著提高了模型在实际应用中的鲁棒性。

title: Anti-causal domain generalization: Leveraging unlabeled data
summary: The problem of domain generalization concerns learning predictive models that are robust to distribution shifts when deployed in new, previously unseen environments. Existing methods typically require labeled data from multiple training environments, limiting their applicability when labeled data are scarce. In this work, we study domain generalization in an anti-causal setting, where the outcome causes the observed covariates. Under this structure, environment perturbations that affect the covariates do not propagate to the outcome, which motivates regularizing the model's sensitivity to these perturbations. Crucially, estimating these perturbation directions does not require labels, enabling us to leverage unlabeled data from multiple environments. We propose two methods that penalize the model's sensitivity to variations in the mean and covariance of the covariates across environments, respectively, and prove that these methods have worst-case optimality guarantees under certain classes of environments. Finally, we demonstrate the empirical performance of our approach on a controlled physical system and a physiological signal dataset.
core_methodology: The paper introduces methods for Domain Generalization (DG) specifically in an anti-causal setting, where the outcome causes the observed covariates. It proposes regularizing the model's sensitivity to variations (mean and covariance) in covariates across different environments, leveraging unlabeled data. This is a novel approach to building robust models against distributional shifts without relying on labeled data from the target domain.
data_sources: The immediate examples use a controlled physical system and a physiological signal dataset. For finance, this methodology would be applied to heterogeneous market data sets (e.g., time series from different market regimes, exchanges, or asset classes) where the underlying causal structure might be complex or unknown.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in creating trading models that are robust to regime changes, market structure shifts, or sudden data drift. Financial markets are notorious for non-stationarity and domain shifts (e.g., regulatory changes, macroeconomic regime shifts). By learning representations invariant to these shifts (by focusing on the anti-causal structure), the resulting alpha decay rate might be significantly reduced compared to standard models that overfit to the training environment. This directly supports building more stable factor models or reinforcement learning agents.
title_cn: 反因果域泛化：利用无标签数据
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种在存在反因果结构下（结果导致协变量）实现领域泛化的新方法，适用于利用无标签数据来构建对市场环境变化（如金融制度、宏观经济周期）不敏感的预测模型。该技术有望提高量化策略的稳健性和长期表现，减少模型在市场结构突变时的阿尔法衰减。

title: Regular Fourier Features for Nonstationary Gaussian Processes
summary: Simulating a Gaussian process requires sampling from a high-dimensional Gaussian distribution, which scales cubically with the number of sample locations. Spectral methods address this challenge by exploiting the Fourier representation and treating the spectral density as a probability distribution suitable for Monte Carlo approximation. Although this probabilistic interpretation is valid for stationary processes, it is overly restrictive for the nonstationary case, where spectral densities are generally not probability measures. We propose regular Fourier features for harmonizable processes to avoid this limitation. Our method discretizes the spectral representation directly, preserving the correlation structure among spectral weights without requiring probability assumptions. Under a finite-spectral-support assumption, this yields an efficient low-rank approximation that is consistent and positive semi-definite by construction. When the spectral density is unknown, the framework extends naturally to kernel learning from data. We demonstrate the method on locally stationary and harmonizable mixture kernels, the latter with a complex-valued spectral density, and apply the kernel-learning extension to real and synthetic data.
core_methodology: The paper proposes 'regular Fourier features' to efficiently approximate nonstationary Gaussian processes (GPs) by directly discretizing their spectral representation. This avoids the problematic probabilistic assumption required when using standard Fourier methods for nonstationary data, yielding a consistent and positive semi-definite, low-rank approximation. The framework also extends to kernel learning from observed data.
data_sources: The method is demonstrated on synthetic data and real time-series data where the underlying correlation structure (kernel) needs to be learned or approximated, such as locally stationary or harmonizable processes.
alpha_potential: Gaussian Processes are powerful tools for time-series forecasting, prediction, and uncertainty quantification. By providing an efficient, scalable method (low-rank approximation) for handling *nonstationary* kernels—a common feature in financial markets where volatility and correlation regimes shift—this technique significantly improves the feasibility of using sophisticated GP models for tasks like dynamic portfolio optimization, risk modeling (e.g., Value-at-Risk estimation), or advanced time-series forecasting where standard stationary assumptions fail. The kernel learning extension is crucial for adapting the model to evolving market conditions.
title_cn: 面向非平稳高斯过程的正则傅里叶特征
summary_cn: 该研究提出正则傅里叶特征，用于高效近似非平稳高斯过程（GPs）。这解决了金融时间序列（如波动率、相关性）中普遍存在的非平稳性问题。通过低秩逼近和核学习，该方法能更稳定、更大规模地应用于动态风险建模、投资组合优化和高精度、考虑不确定性的情景预测中，是先进时间序列预测模型的关键技术改进。

title: Everywhere Valid Bounds on False Discovery Proportions in Conformal Inference
summary: Modern applications of conformal inference to multiple testing problems, such as outlier detection and candidate selection, often involve selecting test samples whose conformal p-values fall below a threshold. The quality of such methods is often measured by the false discovery proportion (FDP), defined as the fraction of incorrect selections. Existing approaches typically control the expected value of the FDP, using methods such as the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. This approach fails to provide high-probability bounds on the realized false discovery proportion and invalidates statistical guarantees if the rejection threshold is selected after inspecting the data. This paper establishes finite-sample, distribution-free upper bounds on the FDP that hold simultaneously over all possible rejection thresholds, enabling arbitrary post hoc selection of the threshold. Simultaneous validity is achieved by constructing a high-probability envelope for the empirical distribution function of null conformal p-values by sampling from their joint distribution. Furthermore, our framework allows practitioners to modulate the envelope's shape, thereby producing tight bounds in rejection regions of primary interest. We use this flexible approach to derive simultaneous FDP upper bounds for both outlier detection and conformal selection. We demonstrate through synthetic and real-data experiments that the resulting bounds are both valid and substantially less conservative than those derived from existing approaches.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel framework for Conditional False Discovery Proportion (FDP) control using Conformal Inference. It provides finite-sample, distribution-free, simultaneous upper bounds on the FDP that are valid across all possible rejection thresholds, even after data inspection. This is achieved by constructing a high-probability envelope for the empirical distribution function of null conformal p-values.
data_sources: The methodology is generally applicable to any data where multiple hypothesis testing or selection is performed, such as general time series data, features used in factor models, or signals derived from market indicators. The paper uses synthetic and real-data experiments, suggesting broader applicability.
alpha_potential: The primary application is risk control and model selection. In quantitative trading, many strategies involve testing numerous hypotheses (e.g., testing thousands of potential factors, selecting optimal portfolios, or identifying significant market regimes/outliers). Traditional methods like Benjamini-Hochberg control the expected FDP, which can be misleading. This research offers statistically rigorous, high-probability guarantees on the proportion of false positives among selected signals or rejected hypotheses. This allows systematic traders to select signals or construct models with much tighter, provable confidence on the error rate, leading to more robust portfolio construction and better risk management, especially in high-frequency or high-dimensionality settings.
title_cn: 一致有效的一致性推断中误发现率的普遍有效界限
summary_cn: 该研究为多重假设检验（如信号筛选或异常检测）提供了基于一致性推断的、严格的误发现比例（FDP）高概率上界。这解决了传统方法在事后选择阈值时统计保证失效的问题。在量化交易中，该方法可用于构建更鲁棒的因子选择和信号验证流程，确保筛选出的有效信号集中的错误率在实际操作中得到可靠的、高概率的控制，从而提升策略的稳健性。

title: Triangular-Reference Schr\"odinger Bridges for Time Series Generation
summary: Schr\"odinger bridges for time series (SBTS) generate synthetic paths by projecting, in relative entropy, a Brownian reference onto the path laws that match the joint distribution of the data on the observation grid. The Brownian reference, however, fixes the quadratic variation of the generated paths, which is restrictive when stochastic volatility, correlated noise, or rank-deficient covariance structures must be reproduced. We introduce "Triangular-Reference Schr\"odinger Bridges for Time Series" (TR-SBTS), which keeps the entropy-projection backbone of SBTS but replaces the Brownian reference by a triangular, volatility-informed, intervalwise frozen reference on a state augmented with latent covariance descriptors. The construction remains a single entropy projection on the augmented state: the minimiser is the \(h\)-transform of the reference, and on each frozen interval the optimal drift has the logarithmic-gradient form \(b^\star(t,x)=A\,\nabla\log H(t,x)\), intrinsic to the active covariance directions when the frozen covariance \(A\) is degenerate. We prove stability of the frozen approximation and consistency of the associated regularised kernel estimators, describe a reference-aware Nadaraya--Watson implementation of the conditional next-increment law, and evaluate the construction on numerical experiments.
core_methodology: Introduces Triangular-Reference Schrödinger Bridges for Time Series (TR-SBTS) to model path distributions. It improves upon standard Schrödinger Bridges by replacing the fixed Brownian reference with a volatility-informed, triangular reference on an augmented state, allowing it to capture complex covariance structures (like stochastic volatility and rank-deficient covariance) more accurately during the entropy projection process.
data_sources: Time series data (e.g., asset prices, returns) used to define the observation grid and joint distribution for path generation.
alpha_potential: The ability to generate synthetic time series that accurately capture complex features like stochastic volatility and correlated noise is highly valuable for derivative pricing, risk modeling (VaR, Expected Shortfall), and scenario analysis for options and volatility trading strategies. It could be used to create more realistic simulation environments for reinforcement learning agents or for stress-testing factor portfolios.
title_cn: 用于时间序列生成的三边参考薛定谔桥
summary_cn: TR-SBTS提出了一种改进的时间序列生成模型，它通过引入考虑波动率的三角参考，克服了传统薛定谔桥模型对二次变差的限制。这使得模型能更精确地捕捉随机波动和复杂协方差结构。该技术对金融衍生品定价、风险管理（如压力测试和VaR计算）以及增强市场模拟的现实性具有重要应用价值。

title: DeXposure-Claw: An Agentic System for DeFi Risk Supervision
summary: Decentralized finance exposes supervisors to fast-moving, networked credit risks. General-purpose LLM agents fit this setting poorly: they over-read weak evidence and recommend high-stakes interventions, while existing evaluations offer no regulator-aligned way to measure the resulting false alarms. We introduce DeXposure-Claw, a forecast-grounded agentic supervision system that routes LLM decisions through structured evidence: (1) DeXposure-FM, a graph time-series foundation model, forecasts future exposure networks; (2) deterministic monitors and stress scenarios then turn those forecasts into typed alerts, attribution signals, and scenario evidence; and (3) data-health and confidence gates constrain escalation before DeXposure-Claw emits auditable supervisory tickets with rationales. We further develop DeXposure-Bench, a six-axis evaluation harness, whose decision axis scores tickets against a regulator-aligned absolute-loss ground truth and an explicit false-intervention rate. Experiments on five years of weekly real data fully support our system. Code is at https://github.com/EVIEHub/DeXposure-Claw.
core_methodology: The system integrates three main components: (1) DeXposure-FM, a graph time-series foundation model designed to forecast future inter-entity exposure networks (credit risk structure). (2) Deterministic monitors and stress scenarios that analyze these forecasts to generate structured alerts and attribution signals. (3) Confidence gates and data-health checks that constrain the intervention process before issuing auditable supervisory tickets. This forms a feedback loop for risk management.
data_sources: Five years of weekly real data related to Decentralized Finance (DeFi) exposure networks, likely comprising transaction graphs, smart contract interactions, and asset flows.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on 'supervision' rather than direct trading, the core predictive component—DeXposure-FM, a graph time-series foundation model forecasting future exposure networks—is highly relevant. This methodology provides advanced foresight into changing systemic credit risk linkages within DeFi. A quantitative trader could use the risk forecasts and resulting stress signals as a predictive feature for risk-on/risk-off portfolio allocation, or to short 'over-leveraged' network structures before market stress materializes. It offers a sophisticated way to model and predict contagion risk.
title_cn: DeXposure-Claw：一个用于DeFi风险监管的代理系统
summary_cn: 该系统提出了DeXposure-Claw，一个用于去中心化金融（DeFi）系统性风险监管的智能代理框架。其核心是DeXposure-FM图时间序列模型，用于预测未来数周的信用风险暴露网络。交易者可借鉴其网络预测和压力信号，将其转化为投资组合的风险因子或用于宏观对冲策略，从而提前规避DeFi领域的系统性流动性/信用风险事件。

title: Gaussian Mixture Attention: Linear-Time Sequence Mixing via Probabilistic Latent Routing
summary: The dense token-to-token interaction pattern of standard dot-product attention remains a central bottleneck in scaling Transformer architectures to long contexts. We introduce \textbf{Gaussian Mixture Attention (GMA)}, a probabilistic attention-style sequence mixer that replaces explicit pairwise query--key comparison with routing through $K$ learned Gaussian mixture components. Queries and keys are mapped to posterior \textit{responsibility} vectors over a shared latent routing space; their overlap defines an implicit responsibility-space affinity, while values are written into and read from a $K$-slot latent memory. By exploiting the associativity of matrix multiplication, GMA avoids materializing the induced $N\times N$ affinity matrix and instead uses two responsibility matrices whose dominant activation storage scales as $\mathcal{O}(NK)$ rather than $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ for fixed $K$. We formulate bidirectional and causal variants of GMA, provide an end-to-end differentiable parameterization of the Gaussian mixture components, and analyze its responsibility-modulated gradient structure, constrained non-negative low-rank affinity interpretation, and local routing stability. Empirically, GMA exhibits the intended fixed-$K$ linear memory scaling and is competitive with attention-style baselines on long-context classification, while causal GMA improves over tested linear/random-feature attention variants on WikiText-103 but remains behind optimized causal SDPA and Mamba in the current implementation. Analysis of learned responsibilities further shows broad component usage and moderate alignment with surface-form token categories, supporting GMA as a probabilistic, interpretable, fixed-$K$ linear-time attention-style alternative rather than a universal replacement for optimized softmax attention or state-space models.
core_methodology: Introduction of Gaussian Mixture Attention (GMA), a mechanism that replaces quadratic $O(N^2)$ dot-product attention with $O(NK)$ linear-time sequence mixing by routing through $K$ learned Gaussian mixture components. It uses probabilistic latent routing to compute sequence affinity implicitly, offering a memory-efficient alternative to standard Transformer attention.
data_sources: Primarily benchmarks standard NLP datasets (e.g., WikiText-103) for sequence modeling performance. For financial application, time-series data (price, volume, order book snapshots) of financial instruments would be the necessary input.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in its efficiency for processing very long sequences of financial data, such as high-frequency order book dynamics or long-term market narratives. Reducing the computational complexity from quadratic to linear in sequence length ($N$) allows for analyzing much longer historical contexts at manageable computational cost, which is crucial for identifying complex, long-range dependencies in market behavior or deriving robust features from extensive text data (e.g., news sentiment over months).
title_cn: 高斯混合注意力：通过概率潜在路由实现线性时间序列混合
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种名为高斯混合注意力（GMA）的新型序列混合机制，将处理长序列的计算复杂度从二次方降至接近线性。在量化交易中，该方法可用于高效分析极长的市场时间序列数据（如高频行情或长期事件序列），捕获更长的市场依赖关系，从而可能用于构建更稳健的因子模型或预测性能更佳的序列预测模型。

title: A Link between Shock-wave Theory and Symmetry-reduced Stochastic Gradient Descent for Artificial Neural Networks
summary: We develop a mathematically explicit link between shock-wave theory and the symmetry-quotiented learning dynamics of stochastic gradient descent, drawing on differential geometry, Lie group theory, and fluid mechanics. Specifically, after quotienting parameter symmetries and applying local-entropy coarse-graining, the effective dynamics satisfy a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation on the quotient manifold. Moreover, under the assumption that the raw parameter dynamics can be summarized by a gradient field on the quotiented space, the gradient of the coarse-grained loss function obeys a Burgers-type equation, and shock formation can be established rigorously. We apply our theory to multilayer perceptrons, convolutional neural networks, Transformers, and mean-field networks, and show that they obey the Hamilton--Jacobi or Burgers-type equations. We conjecture that this framework also yields practical diagnostics for deep learning. In architectures such as Transformers, raw parameter norms are often distorted by symmetry redundancy and may therefore be misleading, whereas symmetry-corrected quotient observables provide a principled basis for monitoring, forecasting, and controlling training-phase transitions.
core_methodology: The research establishes a mathematical link between shock-wave theory (Burgers equation, Hamilton-Jacobi equation) and the dynamics of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) when network symmetries are accounted for (quotient manifold learning). It uses concepts from differential geometry and fluid mechanics to analyze Neural Network training dynamics.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applied to standard deep learning architectures (MLPs, CNNs, Transformers, Mean-Field Networks). No specific financial market data is utilized in the abstract, but the methodology is applicable to models trained on financial time series or alternative data.
alpha_potential: The primary value lies not in immediate alpha generation but in providing 'practical diagnostics for deep learning' by monitoring symmetry-corrected observables. In complex financial models (like Transformers used for forecasting), this framework could offer principled ways to monitor training stability, detect mode collapse due to symmetry redundancy, and forecast training-phase transitions. This leads to more robust and reliable predictive models, indirectly improving strategy performance by enhancing model quality assurance.
title_cn: 人工神经网络中激波理论与对称性规约随机梯度下降的联系
summary_cn: 该研究将流体力学中的激波理论与深度学习的训练动力学联系起来。其主要价值在于为监控和诊断神经网络（如应用于金融预测的Transformer）的训练过程提供了新的理论基础。通过分析对称性规约后的观测值，研究人员可以更可靠地监测训练稳定性、预测模型训练阶段的转变，从而构建更鲁棒的量化预测模型。

title: Starter-Iterator Neural Operator: A Unified Architecture for High-Fidelity Forward and Inverse PDE Problems
summary: Operator learning is an emerging interdisciplinary field that integrates machine learning with scientific computing. By mapping infinite-dimensional function spaces, this approach provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs). Compared to traditional numerical solvers, it achieves a superior trade-off between computational complexity and approximation accuracy, demonstrating significant advantages in many-query tasks such as real-time prediction and parameter sweeps. Given the stringent accuracy requirements of both forward simulation and inverse inference, as well as the precision bottlenecks of existing operator learning methods in handling complex boundaries or long-term evolution, we propose the Starter-Iterator Neural Operator (SINO). Our framework reinterprets the initialization strategies and iterative formats of traditional iterative methods through neural networks, establishing an efficient approach for spectral-spatiotemporal collaborative modeling. Specifically, the frequency-domain initialization module captures globally stable low-frequency features, while the time-domain learning module focuses on optimizing local solution residuals, thereby effectively overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional single-domain modeling approaches. Extensive experiments on typical dynamical systems such as the Navier-Stokes equations and acoustic wave equations, as well as practical applications including super-resolution imaging and weather forecasting, demonstrate that SINO achieves outstanding performance in numerical accuracy, generalization capability, and robustness.
core_methodology: The Starter-Iterator Neural Operator (SINO) proposes a unified architecture for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) by reinterpreting iterative numerical methods using neural networks. It separates global feature capture (frequency-domain initialization) from local residual optimization (time-domain learning) to achieve high-fidelity simulations and inverse problem solving.
data_sources: The abstract focuses on scientific domains (Navier-Stokes, acoustic waves, weather forecasting) rather than direct financial data. However, the methodology could be applied to simulating complex financial systems or processing high-frequency data requiring PDE modeling.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on scientific computing, the core benefit lies in superior, real-time surrogate modeling for complex, high-dimensional systems. In finance, this translates to rapid, accurate pricing of path-dependent derivatives (where Black-Scholes assumptions fail), or highly efficient calibration of complex stochastic volatility models (like Heston or SABR) via inverse PDE methods. The speed and accuracy gains over traditional Monte Carlo or finite difference methods offer a pathway to faster option pricing and risk management in high-throughput environments.
title_cn: 启动器-迭代器神经算子：高保真前向与逆向偏微分方程问题统一架构
summary_cn: SINO提出了一种结合频域初始化和时域学习的神经算子框架，用于高效、高精度地求解复杂的偏微分方程（PDE）。该技术可作为传统数值求解器的快速替代品。在金融领域，它有望实现对复杂路径依赖衍生品的实时报价、高频风险因子计算，以及随机波动率模型的快速校准，显著提升量化交易和风险管理系统的计算效率和精度。

title: Fisher Width: A Geometric Measure of Complexity on Statistical Manifolds
summary: Gaussian width is a central geometric complexity measure in high-dimensional probability, compressed sensing, convex optimization, and learning theory. It quantifies the average extent of a set along random directions, thereby capturing the effective dimension of constraint sets, hypothesis classes, and descent cones. However, this notion is intrinsically Euclidean. Statistical models instead carry a natural Riemannian geometry induced by the Fisher information metric, where directions are scaled according to statistical distinguishability rather than ambient Euclidean length. We introduce Fisher width, a Fisher-geometric analogue of Gaussian width for statistical manifolds. At a parameter point $\theta$, Fisher width replaces the Euclidean identity by the local metric tensor $G(\theta)^{1/2}$, measuring the Gaussian width of the Fisher-rescaled set. This makes the resulting quantity sensitive to local statistical curvature and invariant under smooth reparameterizations. We develop the basic theory of Fisher width, showing that it retains key structural features of Gaussian width, including concentration, metric perturbation stability, and spectral comparison bounds with the Euclidean baseline, while also capturing anisotropic geometric effects invisible to Euclidean measures. As an application, we prove a generalization bound for Fisher-Lipschitz hypothesis classes and propose computable estimators, which we evaluate empirically on MNIST across three model classes. Fisher width is to statistical manifolds what Gaussian width is to Euclidean convex bodies. This work lays the foundation for studying complexity and learning on curved statistical manifolds.
core_methodology: This paper introduces 'Fisher Width,' a novel geometric complexity measure for statistical manifolds, analogous to Gaussian width but using the Fisher Information Metric. It quantifies model complexity by considering the local statistical curvature of the parameter space, moving beyond simple Euclidean norms. The key is replacing the identity matrix with the Fisher metric tensor ($G(\theta)^{1/2}$) when rescaling directions.
data_sources: The primary data context is the statistical modeling of probability distributions (e.g., empirical risk minimization in machine learning). In finance, this methodology could be applied to analyze the complexity of different parametric models fitted to time series data, such as volatility models or factor models.
alpha_potential: The primary alpha potential lies in using Fisher Width as a superior measure for model risk, inductive bias, or generalization capability within complex financial modeling tasks, such as: 1) **Model Selection/Pruning**: Identifying simpler, yet effective, models (lower Fisher Width) that might generalize better out-of-sample compared to overly complex, overfitted Euclidean models. 2) **Adaptive Portfolio Allocation**: Using the change in Fisher Width of the estimated parameter space (e.g., of a factor risk model) as a predictive signal for regime shifts or model instability. 3) **Improving Generalization Bounds**: Applying the derived generalization bounds to sophisticated ML models (like deep neural networks estimating asset returns) to better assess their out-of-sample performance confidence.
title_cn: 费雪宽度：统计流形上的几何复杂度度量
summary_cn: 本文提出了“费雪宽度”，一种基于费雪信息度量的统计流形几何复杂度度量。在量化交易中，该方法可用于评估参数化金融模型（如风险因子模型）的泛化能力和模型风险。通过衡量统计曲率而非欧氏距离，费雪宽度有助于选择更具鲁棒性的模型，提高模型选择和风险控制的精度，从而间接增强策略的长期表现。

title: DRIFT: Refining Instruction Data via On-Policy Data Attribution
summary: Optimizing the training data distribution for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) dictates the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs). While existing data curation methods excel at accelerating training under constrained budgets, they are less suited to elevating the capability upper bound. The challenge here is no longer to identify a smaller subset that preserves performance, but to refine the data distribution toward instances most capable of improving the final model. To address this problem, we explore instance-level data attribution using Influence Functions (IF). We identify that standard IF formulations struggle in this setting due to two structural limitations: a proximity gap caused by off-policy validation targets, and a severe bias towards gradient norm. We propose DRIFT (Data Refinement via On-Policy Influence Functions for Supervised Fine-Tuning). Instead of relying on external reference data, DRIFT utilizes the model's on-policy rollouts as validation targets, which empirically minimizes the parameter proximity gap and better aligns with the local neighborhood assumption of IF. It further applies signed weighting based on trajectory correctness and debiases influence scores against the gradient hacking issue, allowing a small set of validation queries to act as reliable anchors for attributing the full dataset. Experiments on 7B-parameter instruction and reasoning models show that DRIFT consistently raises the performance ceiling on both, outperforming existing data curation baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DRIFT, a novel method for refining instruction tuning data for Large Language Models (LLMs) by using on-policy Influence Functions (IF). It addresses limitations in standard IFs (proximity gap, gradient norm bias) by using model rollouts as validation targets and applying signed weighting based on trajectory correctness to better attribute high-impact data for performance improvement.
data_sources: Instruction tuning data, model rollouts (likely generated through interaction or simulation, not traditional market data).
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on improving LLM capabilities generally, the methodology of using influence functions and 'on-policy' validation to selectively refine training data based on performance contribution has significant potential for finance. Specifically, it could be used to curate high-value data for training financial LLMs used for market analysis, signal generation, or generating robust simulated trading scenarios. By identifying and prioritizing data that leads to better prediction accuracy or better policy convergence in RL trading agents, it could lead to more robust and higher-performing AI trading systems.
title_cn: DRIFT：通过在策略数据归因来改进指令数据
summary_cn: 该研究提出DRIFT方法，利用在策略评估结果（rollouts）优化LLM的指令调优数据选择。此技术可用于高效筛选和优化用于金融LLM训练的高价值数据，提高模型在特定金融任务（如信号生成或策略回测）上的性能上限，从而为开发更强大的金融AI应用提供支持。

title: TRIDENT: Breaking the Hybrid-Safety-Physics Coupling for Provably Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Safe coordination in networked cyber-physical systems forces learning algorithms to simultaneously handle hybrid discrete-continuous actions, hard training-time safety constraints, and physics-governed dynamics. We show that these three features form a directed cycle of biases that defeats any naive composition of off-the-shelf modules, and formalize this as a three-way coupling lemma. We then introduce TRIDENT, the first MARL framework whose three components are co-designed to cancel each leak: a Richardson-Romberg gradient correction reducing Gumbel-Softmax bias from O(tau) to O(tau^2), a Lyapunov-constrained sequential trust-region update enforcing per-iterate feasibility, and a physics-informed residual critic that decomposes value rather than reward. We prove an O~(1/sqrt(K)) convergence rate to a constrained Nash equilibrium and an O(sqrt(K)) cumulative-violation bound. On multi-UAV mobile-edge computing, autonomous intersection management, and a hybrid SMAC variant, TRIDENT cuts training-time violations by 95.5% over MADDPG and 76.3% over MACPO, while improving reward by 13.5% over the strongest unconstrained baseline.
